questions.title: Write Push
questions.text: A stack is stored in the array `Stack[1:20]` with the pointer `Top` (0 when empty). Write a procedure `Push(Item)` that adds an item, or outputs "Stack full" if there is no space.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- check if Top = 20 (1)
- output "Stack full" (1)
- otherwise increment Top (1)
- store Item at Stack[Top] after incrementing (1)
scheme.model_answer:
```pseudocode
PROCEDURE Push(Item : STRING)
    IF Top = 20 THEN
        OUTPUT "Stack full"
    ELSE
        Top ← Top + 1
        Stack[Top] ← Item
    ENDIF
ENDPROCEDURE
```

questions.title: Write Pop
questions.text: Using the same stack, write a function `Pop()` that returns the top item, or returns "Empty" if there is nothing to remove.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- check if Top = 0 (1)
- return "Empty" (1)
- otherwise take Stack[Top] (1)
- decrement Top and return the item (1)
scheme.model_answer:
```pseudocode
FUNCTION Pop() RETURNS STRING
    IF Top = 0 THEN
        RETURN "Empty"
    ELSE
        Item ← Stack[Top]
        Top ← Top - 1
        RETURN Item
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION
```

questions.title: Linear queue problem
questions.text: Explain the problem with a linear queue implemented in a fixed-size array, and how a circular queue solves it.

- After dequeues the front spaces are never reused, so the queue can report full although there is free space (1)

parts.title: Push algorithm
parts.text: Write an algorithm for push(data) that uses is_full() and outputs an error if the stack is full.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- IF is_full() / Top = 8 (1)
- error message (1)
- Top ← Top + 1 (1)
- Books[Top] ← data (1)
scheme.model_answer:
```pseudocode
PROCEDURE push(data)
    IF is_full() THEN
        OUTPUT "Stack overflow"
    ELSE
        Top ← Top + 1
        Books[Top] ← data

```

parts.title: Dequeue algorithm
parts.text: Write an algorithm for dequeue() for this circular queue.

scheme.mark_scheme:
- check Count = 0 → empty message (1)
- take Jobs[Front]; Front ← (Front MOD 5) + 1 (1)
- Count ← Count − 1 and return the job (1)
scheme.model_answer:
```pseudocode
FUNCTION dequeue() RETURNS STRING
    IF Count = 0 THEN
        RETURN "Queue empty"
    ENDIF
    Job ← Jobs[Front]
    Front ← (Front MOD 5) + 1
    Count ← Count - 1
    RETURN Job
ENDFUNCTION
```

summary: Abstract data types; how a stack (LIFO) and a queue (FIFO) work, their operations (push, pop, peek, enqueue, dequeue, is_empty, is_full) and pointers; tracing operations; implementing a stack, a linear queue and a circular queue with an array; overflow and underflow; and where stacks and queues are used.

blocks.content: A **data type defined by the operations** that can be carried out on it and how they behave, **not** by how it is stored. A stack and a queue are ADTs: we know what **push** or **enqueue** do without knowing whether an **array** or a **linked list** is used inside.

items.title: Stack — LIFO
items.content: **Last In, First Out.** Items are added and removed at the **same end**, the **top**. Like a pile of plates: you take the plate that was put on last.

items.title: Queue — FIFO
items.content: **First In, First Out.** Items are added at the **rear (tail)** and removed from the **front (head)**. Like a line at a shop: the first person to arrive is served first.

rows: Adds an element to the **top** of the stack
**Removes** and returns the element on the **top**
Returns a **copy** of the top element **without removing** it
Checks whether the stack is at **maximum capacity** (fixed-size array)

blocks.content: A variable holding the **position of the top item** of the stack. It increases on **push** and decreases on **pop**. When the stack is empty it is 0 (with an array indexed from 1) or −1 (indexed from 0).

items.title: Stack overflow
items.content: Trying to **push** onto a stack that is **full**.

items.title: Stack underflow
items.content: Trying to **pop** from a stack that is **empty**.

blocks.title: Stack trace
blocks.content:
Start empty. `push(5)`, `push(8)`, `push(2)`, `pop()` → returns **2**, `push(7)`, `peek()` → returns **7** (still in the stack), `pop()` → returns **7**.
| Operation | Stack (bottom → top) | Returned | Top pointer |
|---|---|---|---|
| push(5) | 5 | — | 1 |
| push(8) | 5, 8 | — | 2 |
| push(2) | 5, 8, 2 | — | 3 |
| pop() | 5, 8 | 2 | 2 |
| push(7) | 5, 8, 7 | — | 3 |
| peek() | 5, 8, 7 | 7 | 3 |
| pop() | 5, 8 | 7 | 2 |

blocks.title: From one state to another
blocks.content:
State A (bottom → top): **Java, Python, Kotlin**. State B: **Java, C#, C++**.
Operations: `pop()` (removes Kotlin), `pop()` (removes Python), `push("C#")`, `push("C++")`. You can only reach Java by removing everything above it — you **cannot** take an item from the middle.

DECLARE Stack : ARRAY[1:10] OF INTEGER
DECLARE Top : INTEGER
Top ← 0                                  // empty stack

PROCEDURE Push(Item : INTEGER)
    IF Top = 10 THEN
        OUTPUT "Stack overflow"          // full
    ELSE
        Top ← Top + 1                    // move the pointer up first
        Stack[Top] ← Item
    ENDIF
ENDPROCEDURE

FUNCTION Pop() RETURNS INTEGER
    IF Top = 0 THEN
        OUTPUT "Stack underflow"         // empty
        RETURN -1
    ELSE
        Top ← Top - 1                    // move the pointer down
        RETURN Stack[Top + 1]
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION

FUNCTION Peek() RETURNS INTEGER
    RETURN Stack[Top]                    // the pointer does not change
ENDFUNCTION
blocks.caption: Stack in an array of 10 elements

blocks.content:
stack = []
stack.append(5)        # push

top = stack[-1]        # peek → 8
item = stack.pop()     # pop  → 8
print(len(stack) == 0) # is_empty → False

blocks.content: In an array implementation, **pop** only moves the pointer — the old value stays in the array until it is overwritten by the next **push**. The stack contents are only the items **from position 1 up to Top**.

blocks.title: Queue operations
rows: Adds an element at the **rear** of the queue
**Removes** and returns the element at the **front**
Returns a copy of the front element without removing it
Checks whether the queue is empty / full

blocks.content: A queue uses **two pointers**: **Front (head)** — the position of the **next item to leave**; **Rear (tail)** — the position of the **last item added**.

blocks.title: Queue trace
blocks.content:
Start empty. `enqueue(A)`, `enqueue(B)`, `enqueue(C)`, `dequeue()` → returns **A**, `enqueue(D)`, `dequeue()` → returns **B**.
| Operation | Queue (front → rear) | Returned | Front | Rear |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| enqueue(A) | A | — | 1 | 1 |
| enqueue(B) | A, B | — | 1 | 2 |
| enqueue(C) | A, B, C | — | 1 | 3 |
| dequeue() | B, C | A | 2 | 3 |
| enqueue(D) | B, C, D | — | 2 | 4 |
| dequeue() | C, D | B | 3 | 4 |

DECLARE Queue : ARRAY[1:10] OF STRING
DECLARE Front, Rear : INTEGER
Front ← 1
Rear ← 0                                 // empty: Front > Rear

PROCEDURE Enqueue(Item : STRING)
    IF Rear = 10 THEN
        OUTPUT "Queue full"
    ELSE
        Rear ← Rear + 1
        Queue[Rear] ← Item
    ENDIF
ENDPROCEDURE

FUNCTION Dequeue() RETURNS STRING
    IF Front > Rear THEN
        RETURN "Queue empty"
    ELSE
        Front ← Front + 1
        RETURN Queue[Front - 1]
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION
blocks.caption: Linear queue in an array of 10 elements

blocks.content: Each **dequeue** moves Front forward, so the spaces at the **start** of the array are never used again. After 10 enqueues the queue reports **"full"** even if most items have been removed.

A queue in an array where the **pointers wrap round** to the start of the array when they reach the end, so freed spaces at the front are **reused**. A **count** of items (or a comparison of the pointers) shows whether it is empty or full.

DECLARE Queue : ARRAY[1:5] OF STRING
DECLARE Front, Rear, Count : INTEGER
Front ← 1
Rear ← 0
Count ← 0

PROCEDURE Enqueue(Item : STRING)
    IF Count = 5 THEN
        OUTPUT "Queue full"
    ELSE
        Rear ← (Rear MOD 5) + 1          // 5 wraps round to 1
        Queue[Rear] ← Item
        Count ← Count + 1
    ENDIF
ENDPROCEDURE

FUNCTION Dequeue() RETURNS STRING
    IF Count = 0 THEN
        RETURN "Queue empty"
    ELSE
        Item ← Queue[Front]
        Front ← (Front MOD 5) + 1
        Count ← Count - 1
        RETURN Item
    ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION
blocks.caption: Circular queue of 5 elements

blocks.title: Circular queue trace (5 spaces)
blocks.content:
| Operation | Array positions 1–5 | Front | Rear | Count |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| enqueue A, B, C, D | A B C D _ | 1 | 4 | 4 |
| dequeue() → A | _ B C D _ | 2 | 4 | 3 |
| dequeue() → B | _ _ C D _ | 3 | 4 | 2 |
| enqueue(E) | _ _ C D E | 3 | 5 | 3 |
| enqueue(F) | **F** _ C D E | 3 | **1** | 4 |

Rear wrapped from 5 to **1**: (5 MOD 5) + 1 = 1. A linear queue would already be "full".

blocks.title: Priority queue
blocks.content: In a **priority queue** each item has a **priority**; the item with the **highest priority** leaves first, and items with equal priority leave in FIFO order — e.g. urgent jobs in an operating system, or patients in an emergency room.

blocks.title: Where stacks and queues are used
rows: **Print queue** — documents printed in the order sent
Storing **return addresses** and local variables when subroutines are called; **recursion**
**Keyboard buffer** — key presses processed in the order typed
**Scheduling** processes in an operating system (round robin)
**Breadth-first search**; buffering data packets / video streaming
Reversing a list or a word
Call centres, ticket booking, online orders

blocks.title: Checking brackets with a stack
blocks.content: To check `( [ ] ( ) )`: **push** every opening bracket; on a closing bracket **pop** and check it matches. The expression is correct if every pop matches and the stack is **empty** at the end. For `( [ ) ]` the `)` pops `[` — **mismatch**.

blocks.title: Exam-style answers
blocks.content:
**Q: Name the data structure where the item that was added last is removed first. [1]**
**Stack** (1). (Not "LIFO" — name the structure.)

**Q: Stack A (bottom → top): Java, Python, Kotlin. Write the operations to reach Java, C#, C++. [2]**
`pop()`, `pop()` (1); `push("C#")`, `push("C++")` (1).

**Q: Describe how an item is added to a queue implemented in an array. [3]**
Check the queue is **not full** (1); **increase the rear pointer** (wrapping round in a circular queue) (1); store the item at the **position of the rear pointer** (1).

**Q: Explain why a print server uses a queue. [2]**
Documents must be printed in the **order they were sent** (1); a queue is **FIFO**, so the first document sent is printed first (1).

- Popping from the **bottom** of a stack, or dequeuing from the **rear** of a queue.
- Forgetting to **check for full / empty** before push / pop.
- Updating the pointer in the **wrong order** — in a stack push, increase Top **before** storing.
- Writing values without quotes in stack operations, e.g. push(C#) instead of push("C#").
